newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian rail workers begin national strike.
newsitem.headline: Croatian rail workers begin national strike.

text.p: Some 14,000 Croatian rail workers began an indefinite strike on Thursday, state news agency Hina reported.
It said most traffic in the country, save for international and cargo trains, ground to a halt at 1000 local (0900 GMT).
The strikers have vowed to keep rail traffic at a standstill until their demands for a wage increase and safer working conditions are met.
The rail strike follows a wave of protests in Croatia in the past week as senior citizens, teachers and public service workers have come out on the streets to demand pay and pension increases.
Living standards in the former Yugoslav republic have plunged since 1993, when the government launched a harsh stabilisation programme to curb hyperinflation.
